audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagrees across layers on five of seven rows: content win[] is Fizz/Yone/Yone/Skill/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz (identical to the packet levelChart) while full phases[].side is Yone/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yone/Skill/Yone. audit.why: Content and packet agree exactly, so the full layer is the outlier. Kit grounding for the shape: Mortal Steel is a flat 4s and only dashes with a knockup on the second stack, so level 1 is Fizz's; Spirit Cleave lands at 3 on a 14s shield, so 2-3 are Yone's; Chum the Waters plus the string at 6 and first item are Fizz's, and Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved to the content values, ratings adjusted, and every why on both layers rewritten to argue its own verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page describes Soul Unbound as an escape dash — 'Yone's E dash lets him reposition through minions to escape', 'he can flash-E out of a bad spot' — which inverts what it does. It also calls Fate Sealed a 'global-ish execute threat'. Neither matches the kit. The packet also flags that this matchup never names a single Yone ability anywhere in the content layer.
audit.why: Kit: E Soul Unbound, 22/19/16/13/10s — the spirit leaves the body and is FORCED BACK to it when the ability ends, repeating a portion of the damage dealt. That makes it a commitment whose end point is known in advance, which is exactly what a shark wants. R Fate Sealed is 1000 range, 120/100/80s, and blinks him behind the LAST champion in a line, pulling everyone hit — so standing off that line denies it. W Spirit Cleave is 14s and shields more per champion hit.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound described as a commitment with a known return point; Fate Sealed given its real range, cooldown and line requirement; ability names used throughout.

audit.why: Soul Unbound is the tracked cooldown and it halves across ranks, 22s to 10s — a player needs that number to know how long the punish window lasts.
audit.corrected: Written in alongside Mortal Steel's flat 4s and Fate Sealed's 120/100/80s.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 you have the edge with Urchin Strike poke and no-collision positioning that dodges his Q1/Q2 pokes. Yone's E dash lets him reposition through minions to escape or reset your all-in, so don't overextend your first engage. Trade with Q then back off rather than fully committing — he can flash-E out of a bad spot. Both are melee, so watch for his Q3 knockup chaining into extra auto damage.
edits.after: Level 1 you have the edge with Urchin Strike and no-collision positioning that dodges his first two Mortal Steel thrusts. Soul Unbound is not an escape — his spirit is forced back to the body when it ends — so it is a commitment you can punish rather than something he flashes out with. Trade with Q then back off, and watch the second Mortal Steel stack: that is the one that dashes and knocks you up.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 you can bully him hard: Q-AA-W trades win most exchanges since he lacks sustain and your untargetable E dodges his Q3 knockup follow-up. Level 6 flips momentum — his ultimate is a global-ish execute threat that turns any poke exchange into a kill if his jungler is nearby, so respect ganks and don't facecheck brush after using E. Keep wave control tight so he can't freely roam with R.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 lean Yone: Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s and its cone covers the wave, so pick your trades on its cooldown and let Playful/Trickster eat the Q3 knockup follow-up. Level 6 flips back to you — Fate Sealed is 1000 range, not global, and sits on 120s, while your shark plus string is a kill from full. Respect ganks and don't facecheck brush after spending E.

edits.before: By two items the fight is close: Yone's crit/lethality build lets him one-shot squishies through Q3 resets, while your Zhonya's/Riftmaker line gives you burst plus survivability. edits.after: By two items you still get there first: your Zhonya's/Riftmaker line gives burst plus survivability while Fate Sealed has to catch the last champion in a line to work at all. Stand off that line, eat the Q3 knockup with Playful/Trickster, and open with the shark — vision around his 1000-range ult matters more than raw stats here.
